messages:
ashley (support): Heads up — customer 'Clearbox' on Private VPC started seeing intermittent 502s and long tails to /v1/generate from our inference host in their subnet. Began after the control-plane push at ~02:15 UTC.

sneha (eng-infra): Which symptoms exactly? timeouts, tls errors, or backend 502? Any client-side traces?

ashley (support): From the app: intermittent 502 (upstream connection reset) and a lot of requests show +400ms tail latency before failing. Curl to the private VIP sometimes succeeds then RSTs mid-stream. I grabbed a short tcpdump from the inference host ENI (10.0.3.22 -> 10.0.3.45).

ashley (support): ```
20:41:02.123456 IP 10.0.3.22.52548 > 10.0.3.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
20:41:02.124890 IP 10.0.3.45.443 > 10.0.3.22.52548: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, length 0
20:41:02.337001 IP 10.0.3.22.52548 > 10.0.3.45.443: Flags [.], ack 1, win 64240, length 0
20:41:03.512233 IP 10.0.3.45.443 > 10.0.3.22.52548: Flags [R.], seq 1, ack 1, win 0, length 0
```

ben (platform): RST from the remote IP after a period — suggests something in the path is killing the connection after the handshake or after initial data. Any firewall or middlebox inline? Which SG / NACL attached to ENI? Also, is the control plane egress-enforcer running?

ashley (support): Customer says they haven't changed SGs in weeks. I ran `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0abc1234` and grabbed the NACL id. Here's the NACL rules summary they pasted (redacted):

ashley (support): ```
# NACL acl-09f8abcd (entries in eval order)
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 443 from 10.0.0.0/16 -> ALLOW
Rule 110: DENY ALL from 0.0.0.0/0 -> DENY (catch-all)
Rule 120: ALLOW TCP 32768-61000 to 0.0.0.0/0 -> ALLOW (ephemeral)
```

ashley (support): The ordering above is exactly the issue — NACLs are order-evaluated. DENY at 110 precedes the ephemeral allow at 120, so outbound ephemeral ports are getting denied after the new policy was applied.

sneha (eng-infra): Oof. That matches the RST timing — handshake OK (server side port 443), then when server tries to open ephemeral source port back or send larger payloads, the NACL denies and we see reset behavior. Customer's app opens ephemeral client src port 52548 which falls in 32768-61000 but NACL DENY catches because of ordering.

ops-jen (ops): Did the control-plane push reorder rules? We had a rollout of egress-enforcer v2 that auto-inserts a deny-by-default rule for new customers. Looks like it inserted a DENY with priority 110 above the ephemeral allow. I can check the audit log.

devops-bot: egress-enforcer/audit: deploy v2 applied to acct-918 at 02:14:57 UTC — inserted rule id=110 DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0. Trigger: "default-deny-mode" enabled.

ben (platform): Quick mitigation options: 1) reorder the NACL so ephemeral allow is <110, 2) remove the deny rule until we sync allow ranges, or 3) widen the allow at 100 to include the ephemeral range (if acceptable). Which can cust do quickly?

ashley (support): Customer asked for minimal blast radius. They did 1) update NACL ordering to move the ephemeral allow above the DENY. I asked them to test with repeated curl loop.

ashley (support): ```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://10.0.3.45:443/v1/generate; done
```

ashley (support): After reorder: 200 x 50, tails back to normal, no RST. Customer also patched egress-enforcer config to add an allow exception for the 10.0.0.0/16 private subnets to avoid future ordering regressions.

ops-jen (ops): Filed fix: rollback-change in egress-enforcer to not add global DENY above existing allow entries (PR #482). Also adding CI test to validate NACL ordering won't introduce new deny above ephemeral allow.

ben (platform): Thanks — leaving a note: for Private VPC inference hosts we should: verify NACL entries in audit, ensure ephemeral port ranges are always prioritized before default deny, and surface a warning during control-plane pushes when a deny is inserted.

ashley (support): Customer confirmed service healthy and latency back to baseline. Marking resolved. :tada: 

sneha (eng-infra): Nice triage. Save the pcap + audit lines to the ticket for postmortem.
